messages:
Priya R: Heads up, BrightLedger seeing a spike in "deferral" replies from our widget after yesterday's quant canary. They reported it started ~2026-03-16 22:30 UTC.

Alex (BrightLedger): Yep, after your update the support bot started replying 'Sorry, I can't help with that' on basic finance questions. Affects many sessions. Example req: req_bright_01

Jules S: Can you paste the raw bot text and any safety metadata you have? Also which model/variant is the widget calling?

Alex (BrightLedger): Snippet:
User: "How do I submit an expense report?"
Bot: "I'm sorry, I can't assist with that request."

Request payload we send:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rw-infer-14b-quant-canary",
  "input": "How do I submit an expense report?",
  "session_id": "bright-428"
}
```

Priya R: They're on a Dedicated plan; routing flagged to the new quant canary after autoscale. BrightLedger reports deferrals jumped from ~2% to ~17% in a 1h window.

Matt G: Two immediate asks: (1) full response with any safety fields, (2) can CS try the same prompt against baseline (rw-infer-14b-v1) to compare safety scores. I'll also run an internal A/B sweep.

Alex (BrightLedger): One log includes this:
```
response: "I'm sorry, I can't assist with that request."
safety_label: "refusal"
safety_score: 0.79
model: "rw-infer-14b-quant-canary"
req_id: "req_bright_01"
```

runtime-bot: Canary deploy rw-infer-14b-quant-canary started 2026-03-16T22:18:05Z. Rollout=15%, config changes: quantization_profile=aggressive_q4, enable_aggressive_clip=true

Matt G: That "enable_aggressive_clip" flag can shift logits and may push some tokens below safety thresholds. I'll spin up a small evaluation run (policy+finance prompt set) and capture classifier logits (safety_dump=true).

Ingrid L: This is an ARR customerwe should throttle canary traffic to 5% until root cause. Also enable fallback to baseline for their routing if possible.

Priya R: Asked BrightLedger to switch routing back to baseline while we investigate. Shall we recommend immediate rollback on their side?

Matt G: Yes. Recommend rollback for production traffic. Meanwhile I'll run 500-prompt A/B and post refusal-rate delta and top-flipping prompts.

Jules S: If they roll back, capture a sample of the failing prompts before and after for diffs. Also collect widget session replays for last 20 incidents.

Alex (BrightLedger): Rolling back their routing to rw-infer-14b-v1 now. Will upload logs in ~10m. Thanks for quick triage.

Priya R: Ticket CS-4891 created for tracking. @Matt please include median safety_score, refusal-rate, and the examples that flip.

Matt G: Quick run: finance set refusal rate goes from 1.8% (baseline) to 16.4% (canary). Median safety_score increases ~+0.25. Will upload CSV and top-25 flips in ~40m.

runtime-bot: Canary traffic for rw-infer-14b-quant-canary reduced to 5% at 2026-03-17T00:05:12Z per ops request.

Ingrid L: If confirmed, schedule a postmortem and include exact quantization commits and any kernel-level clip changes.

Priya R: BrightLedger says baseline fixes the issue for now. We'll keep them posted and log follow-ups.

Matt G: Next steps: produce logits diffs, inspect top-k/top-p clipping behavior, and test relaxing clip on safety-sensitive routes. Also propose adding a safety-regression check in canary pipeline: refuse-delta >5% blocks rollout.

Jules S: Agreed. Add regression test and a quick alert to SRE when refusal delta spikes for high-ARR customers.

Priya R: Thanks everyone. I'll update CS ticket after Matt posts results. :thumbsup:
